ground_truth.description: toolCall object is created outside the produce() callback and holds a direct reference to msg.tool_input (not a deep copy). When this object is pushed into the Solid.js store via produce(), the store wraps it in a reactive proxy, but msg.tool_input remains the original mutable reference. If the WebSocket message handler or any upstream code later modifies msg.tool_input, it will silently mutate the store state without triggering reactivity, causing stale UI.

Accessing state.messages[idx] outside of a tracked context (batch doesn't create a tracking scope) to read toolCalls.length for the ID. In Solid.js, reading store properties outside of createEffect/createMemo/JSX doesn't subscribe to updates. More critically, if another tool_call arrives between this read and the produce() execution, the length-based ID will be wrong (duplicate IDs).

The resultCache is constructed via spread ({ ...(state.messages[idx] as any).resultCache || {} }) which is a shallow copy. The inner objects ({output, is_error}) are new, so this particular spread is safe. However, assigning resultCache inside produce() replaces the entire cache object, breaking any existing reactive subscriptions to individual cache entries in the Solid.js store.

task.title: Key Claude tool results by tool_call_id and carry per-call metadata in claudeStore
task.description: `createClaudeStore` in `gui/src/stores/claudeStore.ts` resolves an incoming `tool_result` back to its call by tool name plus `status === 'pending'`, which breaks down as soon as results come back in a different order than the calls went out. Record the sidecar-supplied `metadata` on the `ToolCallInfo` pushed for each `tool_call` message (defaulting to `{}` when the message carries none), and maintain a `resultCache` on the owning assistant message, keyed by the result's `tool_call_id` and holding `{ output, is_error }`. Extend the `ToolCallInfo`/`AssistantMessage` types to match. Observable outcome: the chat transcript can look a result up by the id of the call it belongs to instead of scanning `toolCalls`, so a turn with several outstanding tool calls renders each call's own output and error state, and per-call metadata is available to the tool-call renderer.
task.test_strategy: Extend `gui/src/__tests__/claudeStore.test.ts` to drive `handleOutboundMessage` through a turn that emits several `tool_call` messages before any result and then delivers the `tool_result` messages in a different order; assert each cached entry carries the `output` and `is_error` of its own call, and that `metadata` from the `tool_call` message reaches the stored `ToolCallInfo` (including the empty-metadata default). Assert the transcript still renders correctly after the turn completes. Run `npm run test` and `npm run typecheck` in `gui/`.
